newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-ZURBRIGGEN TAKES SECOND WIN OF HER CAREER.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ZURBRIGGEN TAKES SECOND WIN OF HER CAREER.

text.p: Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen captured her second career World Cup victory on Saturday, in the third attempt to stage a downhill at this Austrian resort.
The 29-year-old Zurbriggen overcame the poor visibility on the 3,010-metre long Strohsack piste to post a winning time of one minute 42.33 seconds.
Zurbriggen, younger sister of the highly successful Pirmin, previously won a downhill in Lillehammer, Norway, in 1996.
Germany's Hilde Gerg was second in 1:42.69, while Austria's Stefanie Schuster was third in 1:43.06 for her first-ever appearance on a World Cup podium.
The first downhill at Bad Kleinkirchheim, scheduled earlier on Saturday, had to be called off because of heavy fog after nine skiers had completed their runs.

World Cup officials had scheduled two downhills for Saturday after fog had forced them to halt one race on Friday after seven racers. Friday's race was itself meant to be the replacement for a downhill which had to be called off in Crans Montana, Switzerland, in December.
